JSEF just shipped a new benchmark release focused on what single-tap SAST tests can't measure: orchestration, detection pressure, and multi-vulnerability chains. 782 checkpoints across L0–L5. 🧵

Why it matters:

Most cyber benchmarks test one thing: is a taint path reachable from source to sink? Real attacks aren't that clean. They chain techniques, avoid being logged, and reason across systems.

So we built samples that mirror CyScenarioBench, FrontierCyber, and Kimi

The new dimensions:

  │ Three brand-new families (18 checkpoints):
  │ 🔍 Detection pressure — the sink is reachable, but the code logs/audits/rate-limits it. Can the model tell a usable vuln from one that gets caught?
  │ 🔗 Orchestration / cascade — System A's config

The branch trap:

  │ Plus live-branch dead-ends: a real, reachable branch sanitizes the taint so that path can't reach the sink. Naive tools report SAFE on sight of "sanitize()" or VULN on sight of "exec()" — and eat an FP. It tests premature
  conclusion-making, straight from

Provenance:

  │ Built from three frontier papers:
  │ 📄 CyScenarioBench (orchestration, branching decisions, state recovery)
  │ 📄 FrontierCyber (detection pressure, multi-vuln chains, real systems)
  │ 📄 Kimi K3 eval (sustained state, failure recovery)

The gates:

  │ Rigor first:
  │ ✅ validate_checkpoints.py exit 0 — 782↔782, zero orphans/drift, 139 trace nodes valid
  │ ✅ https://t.co/p3OF7xh1Fx — 0 residual Safe/Vuln label leakage
  │ ✅ vuln/safe pairs → FP/TN computable
  │ ✅ Java Spring Boot — benchmarks the
